current_evidence: The council's 'Local planning application requirements' page links this PDF and states 'It was adopted in December 2023 and reviewed in December 2025 when it was decided that no change was required'; the PDF text says 'Adopted 12 December 2023'.

issues.detail: The list date is recorded as 2023-12-01, but the Date basis Grokbot cites and the document text both say it was adopted on 12 December 2023.
The list is flagged 'Outdated (>2y)? Yes', but the council reviewed it in December 2025 and confirmed that no change was needed. It is the current list, re-uploaded in the 2025-12 folder.
issues.evidence: Requirements page: 'reviewed in December 2025 when it was decided that no change was required'.

issues.detail: The 'Planning page' field is the council homepage (https://www.n-somerset.gov.uk) instead of the local planning application requirements page.

These Part 1 items are not captured: Accessible Housing Statement (6+ new residential units, including conversions and changes of use); Amendments Proposed Statement (non-material or minor material amendments); Coal Mining Risk Assessment (Development High Risk Areas, excluding householder, LBC, adverts, LDCs, tree works, prior notifications and insignificant groundworks); Ecological Impact Assessment (where the ecological checklist indicates one, or protected habitats or species may be harmed); Employment Led Statement (10+ dwellings in the J21 Enterprise Area, or 50+ elsewhere in Weston-super-Mare); Sustainability Statement (major development); Flood Warning Evacuation Plan (hazardous substances consent, and FRA sites that are major, vulnerable-persons housing, flats without upper-floor access, camping or caravan sites, or hotels and hostels); Flood Risk Exception Test (highly vulnerable development in FZ2, essential infrastructure in FZ3a/3b, more vulnerable development in FZ3a); Foul Sewerage and Utilities Assessment (100+ dwellings or 10,000m2); Groundwater protection details (Source Protection Zone sites with non-mains drainage, contaminating non-residential uses, contaminated land; excluding householder); Historic Park and Garden Landscape Assessment; Preliminary Bat Roost Assessment (where the ecological checklist confirms one is needed); Retail Sequential Test (retail of 200m2+ outside a defined centre, over 500m2 in a district centre, over 300m2 in a local centre, or additions in a retail park).

These Part 2 plans and drawings are not captured: Location plan (always); Layout plan, existing and proposed (always); Vehicle tracking plan (10+ dwellings); Floor plans - existing (extensions, replacement dwellings, Green Belt replacements, changes of use); proposed floor plans showing wheelchair turning areas (retirement and supported independent living); Elevations (new buildings, extensions, external alterations, advertisements); Sections and levels (sloping or uneven sites, or significant level changes); Joinery details (new or replacement windows or doors on heritage buildings in a conservation area, and internal joinery for LBC).

The Householder 'Ecological Survey' row's trigger is actually the Coal Mining Risk Assessment trigger, and householder development is listed there as an exemption, not as an application type that needs it. The real householder ecology item is the Ecological checklist (all applications except adverts, LDCs, changes of use with no works, and NMAs) and an EcIA where the checklist indicates one.
issues.evidence: Excerpt: 'Required for all development in Development High Risk Areas, excluding those on the Exemptions List e.g.: Householder development'.

issues.detail: The 'Archaeological Assessment' row is placed under Advertisement consent because the excerpt names 'Advertisement Consent'. That text is the Ecological checklist exclusion list, so advertisements are excluded. The Archaeological Desk Based Assessment is required for development within an archaeological site or Scheduled Monument site and does not apply to adverts.
issues.evidence: Excerpt: 'Ecological checklist Required for all planning applications except for applications for: Advertisement Consent'.

issues.detail: Floor plans and Telecommunication Information are placed under 'Change of use - prior approval'. The floor-plans trigger ('proposals for a change of use') refers to change-of-use planning applications. Telecommunication Information applies to all telecoms development, not to change-of-use prior approvals.
issues.evidence: PDF Part 2 item 7: 'Required for all new buildings, extensions to existing buildings and proposals for a change of use'; Part 1 item 33: 'Required for all telecoms development'.

issues.detail: Triggers are cut off before the thresholds. Energy Statement reads 'Required for: 1.' (actual: all new residential units including conversions, and non-residential development over 500m2). Flood Risk Assessment reads 'Required for: Flood Risk Sequential Test Evidence Required for: 1.' (actual: 1ha+ in FZ1, FZ2/3, other flood sources, future risk in the SFRA). Heritage Statement reads 'Required for: 1.' (actual: LBC, listed building or curtilage, conservation area, registered park or garden, HER assets). Open Space reads '...1.' (actual: major development of 10+ dwellings or 1,000m2 causing loss of open space, or any loss of a playing field). Health Impact Assessment runs into the Heritage Statement text and omits the thresholds (200+ dwellings or 4ha; non-residential 10,000m2 or 2ha). LVIA's trigger is the Land Contamination text (actual: major development with buildings outside settlement boundaries, or structures significantly taller). Drainage gives only limb 2 of 4 (actual: major; Neighbourhood Plan requirement; minor development in flood-prone areas or FZ2/3; minor development increasing flood risk; excluding householder).

Some rows are mapped to text that does not support them. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' uses the Arboricultural Method Statement sentence from the Tree Survey item. 'Waste / Refuse and recycling storage' uses the CMRA list of insignificant groundworks ('bin stores and smoking shelters...'); neither is an item in the list. The 'CIL Additional Information' trigger is a policy citation plus a use-class fragment. The Retail row merges the Retail Impact Assessment and Retail Park Justification triggers.
issues.evidence: Grokbot trigger_excerpts compared with PDF Part 1 items 7, 8, 31, 32, 36.

issues.detail: About 26 rows are tagged 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', yet the source often states applicability explicitly. Examples: CIL Form 1 applies to full, householder, reserved matters, LDC, S106 modification, prior approval and technical details applications, but NOT outline. Heritage Statement and Joinery details apply to Listed building consent, which is shown as '(none)'. The Amendments Proposed Statement applies to non-material and minor material amendments, shown as '(none)'. The Flood Warning Evacuation Plan applies to hazardous substances consent, shown as '(none)'. The Ecological checklist applies to every type except adverts, LDCs, changes of use with no works and NMAs, so it covers householder, outline, reserved matters and LBC.
issues.evidence: PDF item 8: CIL 'Not required for outline, minerals or waste applications'; item 22: Heritage Statement 'Listed building consent'; item 5 exclusions.

issues.detail: The only tab item is mostly a list of legislation and policy citations ('Wildlife & Countryside Act 1981 ... NPPF - Paragraph 192 ... Core Strategy - Policy CS4') attached to one sentence. The app-type row built from it is mislabelled 'Validation checklist form (completed)' when the item is actually the Ecological checklist with defined exclusions.
issues.evidence: PDF item 5 'Ecological checklist' with policy-driver column.

summary: Grokbot's link is the current list: adopted 12 Dec 2023 and reviewed in Dec 2025 with no change. The date is slightly wrong and the list is wrongly flagged as outdated. Grokbot missed about 13 of the 37 Part 1 items and most Part 2 drawings, attached several triggers to the wrong items (notably the householder and advert rows, where it read exclusions as inclusions), and cut off most thresholds.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
